proof.text: Choose a minimal finite generating set of the maximal ideal with cardinality its spanFinrank. Regularity identifies that number d with dim B. Enumerate it by Fin d. The existing regular-local generator theorem proves regularity of the resulting list, without coefficient coordinates or completeness.

Apply the prime-field polynomial parameter-map regularity lemma to the chosen tuple. Install the evaluation P-algebra structure on B. Popescu gives a small filtered diagram of smooth P-algebras with the specified ring colimit.

Use Mathlib IsFiltered.exists_directed, which already returns a partial order and a final functor. Restrict scalars on each P-algebra to k and whisker along this functor. The structure maps give τ, the Popescu cocone gives β, and P-linearity gives β_a∘τ_a=aeval t. Finality preserves the specified ring colimit. No preorder-to-poset replacement is needed.

Apply the parameter-quotient diagram theorem to the supplied smooth diagram and colimit. It constructs normalized quotient stages and their residue colimit, and proves every stage regularity, regular-sequence, smoothness and codimension assertion.

If an integer ℓ is a unit in B, its image in k is nonzero: otherwise its image in B would be zero. Its inverse exists in the field k and maps to an inverse in every k-algebra C_a. This argument works for every field k and does not need primality of ℓ.

title: Smooth polynomial-parameter models of an equicharacteristic complete regular local ring
statement:
Let $k_0$ be $\mathbf Q$ or $\mathbf F_p$ for a prime $p$. Let $(B,\mathfrak n)$ be a nonzero Noetherian regular local $k_0$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-regular-scheme], complete for $\mathfrak n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and let $d=\dim B$ and $F=B/\mathfrak n$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring, def-weil-residue-field]. There are generators $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of $\mathfrak n$ and a small nonempty directed poset $I$ with a directed system of commutative $P=k_0[T_1,\ldots,T_d]$-algebras $C_a$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and compatible $P$-algebra maps $C_a\to B$, where $T_i\mapsto t_i$, with the following properties. Each $\operatorname{Spec}C_a\to\operatorname{Spec}P$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Every $C_a$ and $D_a=C_a/(T_1,\ldots,T_d)C_a$ is a nonzero regular Noetherian ring. The images of $T_1,\ldots,T_d$ form a $C_a$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], preserved by every transition map. The quotient $\operatorname{Spec}D_a$ is smooth over $k_0$ and the closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}D_a\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}C_a$ has constant codimension $d$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-per-regular-closed-immersion-codimension]. The specified maps induce isomorphisms of rings
$$\varinjlim_a C_a\xrightarrow{\sim}B,\qquad\varinjlim_a D_a\xrightarrow{\sim}F,$$
and the second is the quotient of the first by the parameters, identifying the limiting immersion with $\operatorname{Spec}F\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}B$. The $t_i$ form a $B$-regular sequence. If a prime $\ell$ is invertible in $B$, then $\ell$ is invertible in every $C_a$. This includes $d=0$, with empty parameters and $D_a=C_a$.
